purpose: Refine Experiment B's validated parameter partition into mechanistic subgroups and test whether the FWR-dominant expert-output-drift contribution aligns with the pre-FWR historical retention direction mu_g.

protocol_identity.pairs: all 28 unordered expert pairs from 8 experts

t4_batch_contract.selection: filter original CIFAR100 train targets to classes 80..99, preserve filtered order, take positions 0:255

groups.Z_downstream: final norm/head and other parameters downstream of the L1 A-live frame

counterfactual_construction.gradient_source: the exact same forced-pair incoming-task loss used by validated Experiment B
counterfactual_construction.independence: each group X is perturbed independently from the same theta_k
counterfactual_construction.upstream_rule: apply the group-restricted perturbation only to a shadow model, then recompute the full replay forward so H'_X and G'_X are allowed to move
counterfactual_construction.gate_measure: pre-update natural G_k is the weighting measure for every X
counterfactual_construction.measure_lock: G'_X is never used as the weighting measure in deltaE_X
counterfactual_construction.r_l1_structural_zero: For X=R_L1, H'_X=H_k and all L1 expert parameters are unchanged, so deltaE_R_L1 is exactly zero; record NOT_EVALUABLE when ||deltaE_R_L1|| < 1e-12

first_order_attribution.q: mean_h[ sum_{e in forced_pair} G_k(e,h) * <E_e(theta_k,H_k(h)), mu_hat_k> ]
first_order_attribution.D_total: sum_X D_X; structural-zero groups are exact-zero audit rows
first_order_attribution.dominant_absolute_count: count of cell-steps where |D_X| is the largest absolute group magnitude among non-structural groups

mechanistic_bridge.rationale: The subgroup with the largest accumulated absolute FWR change is tested against the independently defined mu_g historical retention direction.
mechanistic_bridge.decision_rule_1: top-D_X group aligned => mechanism chain supported at the identified subgroup, subject to all audit guardrails passing
mechanistic_bridge.decision_rule_2: top-D_X group orthogonal AND a smaller-D_X group aligned => FWR-dominant change is not retention-relevant; the proposed chain breaks at the subgroup-output bridge
mechanistic_bridge.decision_rule_3: all evaluable groups orthogonal => retention direction is not represented by the tested expert-output-drift pathway in this branch
mechanistic_bridge.decision_rule_4: top-D_X group weakly aligned => weak alignment only; do not claim full mechanistic support
mechanistic_bridge.decision_rule_5: top-D_X group anti-aligned => FWR-dominant group moves opposite the retention direction
mechanistic_bridge.causal_scope: alignment is a mechanistic bridge test, not causal proof of retention improvement
mechanistic_bridge.negative_result_policy: a non-aligned dominant subgroup falsifies the current unified mechanism chain at the tested resolution; it does not prove another mechanism is causal

near_zero_rules.mu_g_norm: if ||mu_g,k|| < 1e-12, mark INVALID_MECHANISTIC_BRIDGE and do not compute cos_X
near_zero_rules.deltaE_norm: if ||deltaE_X|| < 1e-12, mark NOT_EVALUABLE and do not compute cos_X
near_zero_rules.denominator: never divide by a value below 1e-12
near_zero_rules.r_l1: expected NOT_EVALUABLE by construction and is not a bridge failure

trajectory_state_invariants: The canonical trajectory model is mutated only by its direct SGD update.
All counterfactual perturbations occur only on the separate shadow model.
The shadow is synchronized to theta_k before group counterfactuals.
The perturbed shadow group is restored before the next group.
Counterfactual forwards use labels=None and router observation/state updates disabled.
The canonical forced-pair trajectory remains the validated Experiment B trajectory.
